title: Manchester City Face Haaland Doubts as Liverpool Surge
body:
BBC Sport reports that Erling Haaland is considering leaving Manchester City [S1]. A striker of that calibre hearing exit whispers is the kind of story that unsettles a dressing room before a ball is kicked.

The wider gossip is busy. BBC Sport also says Liverpool are exploring a deal for Jamal Musiala [S1], and Manchester United are eyeing Maxi Araujo [S1]. Elsewhere, Manchester United and Manchester City are competing for Chelsea defender Malo Gusto [S2], while Leeds United are pursuing Will Lankshear [S2]. Everyone wants a bargain, and when rivals circle the same targets, patience becomes a harder sell.

The form guide should set the mood. Our Football-Data.co.uk record shows Manchester City with one win, one draw and three defeats from their last five league games, a run that has brought four points, six goals scored and nine conceded [ST1]. Liverpool's last five tell a different story: four wins and one defeat, 12 points from 11 goals scored and three conceded [ST2]. One side is building momentum while the other is leaking goals and points, and that gap explains why every rumour about a departure carries extra weight.

The smart money is on patience.

The Touchline Take: judge the business when the window shuts, not before.
